quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Stopping too often.
Stopping suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires cannot clear water from the road as well. If you go too fast, your tires may lose grip and your car will slide on water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: When turning left from a multi-lane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multi-lane streets and highways.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Faster driving makes your tires less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slower driving makes the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Faster driving makes your tires less effective.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less your tires can wipe away water. If you drive too fast, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane, sliding on water.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or letters. They alert drivers to hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as what?

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: At a flashing red light, you must stop completely and let all traffic that doesn't have to stop go first.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and could run in front of your car without looking.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or upset, they should:

options.text: Drive the same way they normally would.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness can distract you from driving. Your mind is focused on other things instead of the road. Take time to relax and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: How can you avoid a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.
Flash your lights at them.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Stay away from driving alongside them and do not tailgate them.

questions.question: When will you get a point accumulation advisory letter?

options.text: When you have too many points taken off your record.
When you get four points in 12 months.
When you do not score enough on your driving test.
When you fail the written test.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you get four points in 12 months.
questions.explanation: You will get an advisory letter if you reach four points in 12 months. If you reach eight or more points in 18 months, your license will be suspended.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop immediately and block their path.
Do everything you can to clear a path for them.
Signal when it is safe for them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear a path for them.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, make every effort to give it a clear path. If safe, pull to the side of the road to let it pass.

questions.question: If you are convicted of DWI for the first time, what happens?

options.text: Your license is suspended for 90 days.
You are fined $50.
You must install an Ignition Interlock Device (IID).
You get a warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license is suspended for 90 days.
questions.explanation: A first DWI conviction results in a 90-day license suspension. A court conviction can also lead to up to six months in jail and a $500 fine. Penalties are stricter for repeat offenses.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
You react more slowly to hazards.
You drive faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction time to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires at proper air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your car slides on a layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign tell you?

options.text: There is a hazard ahead or nearby.
There is a school zone ahead.
There is a recreation area ahead.
Food and gas are coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a hazard ahead or nearby.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you about hazards. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
Watch for drunk drivers.
There is a dangerous curve ahead.
There is a bump in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. This sign tells you the pavement becomes slippery when wet, making it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: When must you stop at an intersection?

options.text: When you see a flashing red light.
When you see a steady yellow light.
When you see a yellow arrow.
When you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check both directions, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
You can drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when visibility is reduced to 500 feet or less. Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

questions.question: When can you park on the freeway shoulder?

options.text: If you turn on your four-way flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on the freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so others know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers can see your intentions in advance.

questions.question: What must you do when an approaching train is a danger?

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Do not cross until the train has completely passed.
Cross at your own risk.
Find another route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you cannot cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends.
No right turn.
Slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a lane is ending. You need to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle by using the shoulder of the road?

options.text: When the vehicle in front of you is turning left.
To pass a slow-moving vehicle.
Never.
When traffic is blocked for up to 250 feet ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. Other drivers do not expect vehicles there. They may pull off the road without checking.

questions.question: Your license will be suspended if you:

options.text: Refuse to take a chemical test.
Drive 10 mph over the speed limit.
Honk your horn in a residential area after midnight.
Do not dim your high beam lights around another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Refuse to take a chemical test.
questions.explanation: When you drive on public roads, you agree to take a chemical test if a police officer asks. This test checks your blood alcohol level. If you refuse, your license will be suspended for one year.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children, you should:

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: You find a vehicle defect that could affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.
Drive slower.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that affects safe driving must be fixed right away. Fix it before you drive the vehicle.
